sources.fact: On 15 October 2024 Cabinet agreed community consultation on the future of Colne and Mersea Houses at Harts Lane Estate.
The preferred Council option was demolition of Colne and Mersea Houses with future estate regeneration.
Cabinet approved an estimated £15.384m demolition budget, subject to the community consultation outcome.
The decision was published 16 October 2024 and effective from 24 October 2024.
Council meeting records describe Colne and Mersea as two 17-storey blocks, each comprising 100 properties.
The decision purpose records combustible cladding and other fire-protection deficiencies requiring major external and internal works consideration.
Cabinet delegated authority for contracts and ancillary agreements needed to implement the approved proposals.
LBBD's current One Borough Voice building-safety page continues to publish Colne/Mersea safety updates and links the October 2024 Cabinet decision.
The current Harts Lane estate-engagement page records delivered estate improvements and identifies Harts Lane as an active council housing estate context.
LBBD currently identifies a Landlord Services Manager for Harts Lane estate; this supports current estate-management context, not redevelopment permission.
Regulation 19 agenda HTML lists XC - Harts Lane Estate as a site-allocation attachment, verifying allocation provenance without importing PDF detail.
The Colne/Mersea future-options issue is recorded as an approved key decision concerning the two blocks; it is not an approval for whole-estate residential redevelopment.

examples.result: The 2024 decision is a consultation/preferred-demolition decision for Colne and Mersea, not whole-estate planning permission.
£15.384m is a conditional demolition budget and is not converted into residential delivery value.
Two 100-property tower blocks are not treated as the boundary or capacity of the whole XC allocation.
Fire-safety works and current building management are not evidence that redevelopment has received planning consent.
Future estate regeneration language is strategic/governance evidence, not an exact current residential application.
Regulation 19 HTML verifies XC allocation provenance but no inaccessible PDF capacity is imported.
Council landlord/estate-management context is not HMLR title/proprietor evidence.
Promotion remains zero until exact whole-site case, parcel/title relation and statutory overlays are verified.
